findings.text: Top level inode access check runs ordered stages: superblock writability gate, immutable and unmapped identity gates for write requests, filesystem or generic discretionary check, then device and security gates. First failure short circuits and later stages do not run.

Fast permission dispatch prefers a filesystem specific permission hook when the inode has not yet been marked fast. If no hook exists it permanently marks the inode fast and falls through to the generic discretionary evaluator.

Generic discretionary evaluator first tries mode and ACL evaluation. On access denial it applies capability overrides: directories allow read search override for non write and override for write; non directories narrow the request to read write execute and allow read search override for pure read plus override for non execute or when any execute bit is present.

Mode and ACL check provides a cheap all bits granted path when requested low bits are present for user group other and no ACL handling applies. Otherwise owner requests are judged from owner mode bits alone, group ACL entries are consulted when enabled and group mode is non empty, then group membership selects group versus other mode bits.

ACL fetch helper has two modes. Non blocking mode only uses already cached entries and reports retry or child restart when absent or uncached. Blocking mode fetches or creates a cache entry and evaluates it, propagating fetch errors and reporting retry when no ACL exists.

POSIX ACL evaluator considers only read write execute wants and walks entries in order: owner object, named users, owning group and named groups with found tracking, mask, and other. Named and group matches are limited by a following mask entry; other grants only when no group matched; unknown tags and exhausted walks are input output errors.

Cached ACL access selects one of two per inode slots for access versus default. Read copy update readers either return a stable referenced entry or an uncached marker. Replacement duplicates the new entry and releases the prior stable entry while leaving uncached markers unmanaged.

Identity translation maps kernel identities into mount view identities. No operation maps preserve the input, invalid maps yield invalid results, initial namespace uses raw values while other namespaces convert through the filesystem namespace first, unrepresentable values yield invalid results, otherwise the value passes through the mount down mapping.

Attribute change orchestrator validates permission, rejects symlink mode changes, clears a security suppression flag for setuid setgid modes, normalizes unset timestamps to current time with filesystem truncation, handles privilege killing and setuid setgid stripping, validates uid gid mappings, runs security and delegation steps, then delegates to filesystem or simple setattr and emits change and post setattr notifications on success.

Backing file creation allocates a container, initializes the embedded file with supplied flags and credentials, marks it backing and unaccounted, zeroes the stored user path and security state, and runs allocation hooks. Opening then pins the user path, records it in the new file, opens the real path into it, and releases on failure.
Public file open binds the supplied path into the file and opens the dentry. On success it emits an open notification to balance the close notification that release will emit.
Path reference helper acquires one reference on both the mount and the dentry members of a path object.

Filesystem notification mapping translates attribute validity flags into event classes: identity and mode changes map to attribute change, size and mtime map to modify, atime maps to access, combined atime plus mtime maps to attribute change, and no event is sent when no mapped flag is present.

Promotion to fast permission is guarded by the inode spin lock so the flag is set exactly once for the inode lifetime. ACL cache readers hold read copy update protection and only return entries whose reference count could be raised, retrying when promotion races with release. Cache slot replacement and sentinel installation use atomic exchange primitives.

Attribute changes require the target inode to already be locked by the caller. The implementation asserts this precondition on entry and treats setuid setgid flag clearing as protected by the inode write semaphore.

Write access is denied for immutable inodes and for inodes whose owner or group has no mount mapping. Write access to regular files, directories and symlinks on a read only superblock is denied as read only filesystem. Read only state is the superblock read only flag.

Changing the mode of a symlink is rejected as unsupported. Requesting both explicit mode change and implicit setuid setgid killing in one attribute update is a fatal programming error. Pure setuid setgid kill requests with no other effective change complete without calling lower layers.

Attribute updates require that new uid gid values map in the superblock user namespace and that existing uid gid values already be valid unless they are being changed. Violations fail as value overflow.

POSIX ACL handling is enabled either by superblock feature flag or forced off by build configuration. The no ACL fast path reports true when the cached access entry pointer is empty, or unconditionally true when ACL support is not built.

Delegation breaking has two build dependent behaviors. One variant inspects lease context with ordering protection and only invokes lease breaking when a lease list is non empty, with a nonblocking wrapper that captures the inode on would block. The other variant always reports success without action.

Each inode carries two ACL cache slots selected by type: access and default. Entries move among empty, stable referenced, negative cached, and transient uncached sentinel values. The sentinel is derived from the current task address plus one and always tests as uncached.

A backing file embeds a regular file plus a stored user path copy and an opaque security pointer. Simple attribute application optionally resizes the inode, copies prepared attributes into the inode, and marks the inode dirty.

Blocking ACL acquisition states are: cached stable return immediately; uncached without filesystem ACL support return absent; otherwise install a per task sentinel if the slot still shows not cached, fetch from dentry or inode operations, remove the sentinel and propagate errors on fetch failure, create a negative cache entry when no fetch operation exists, else cache a duplicate only if the sentinel is still present.

Setattr timestamp states are: explicitly set values are truncated to filesystem granularity; unset atime ctime mtime each default to the same sampled current time. Privilege states are: consult the need kill hook and drop the kill request when it reports none; expand setuid setgid kills into mode changes conditioned on current mode bits.

Read copy update ACL mode must never invoke blocking fetch operations. A filesystem hook result indicating do not cache is evaluated directly in that mode, while a persistent uncached marker forces the caller to retry outside read copy update.

Requesting an ACL type other than access or default is a fatal programming error. Concurrent ACL readers must cope with reference promotion failure by releasing read protection, relaxing, and retrying rather than using a dying entry.

Permission and attribute outcomes use distinct negative results: access denied for discretionary failure, operation not permitted for immutable, read only filesystem for read only superblock writes, restart or retry indicators for uncached read copy update ACL fetches, input output error for malformed ACLs, value overflow for unmapped identities, and unsupported operation for symlink mode change.
